market.summary: Peru offers national/public networks, substantial public/private university systems and research libraries. This feasibility-selected sample supports multiple Koha deployments, plus Enterprise/Symphony, Alma/Primo, PMB, AbsysNet, Sophia and Quibuk; it establishes no national market-share percentages. Public catalog access and visitor borrowing are separate. Repositories/ALICIA and subscribed ebooks are not physical-book inventories.
market.platform_strategy: Start with policy-cleared Koha UNCP/UNSCH/UNSA and optionally specialist MALI; add a Quibuk adapter for UNSM. SNB offers the strongest prospective public-library reach but its API was access-denied here. The four-university Consorcio shared-search route is strategically valuable but queried Enterprise/Primo origins prohibit search automation. No product integration is authorized or completed in this research.

limitations: Five observed institutions: four selected, one smaller specialist reserve. Six selected targets short of ten; reserves do not fill shortfall.
No national largest-ten ranking established. Numerical units/dates differ; four selected university systems rely on sourced institutional proxies rather than numerical collection totals.
One or two bounded title searches and selected details, not full reliability or adapter certification. Public availability snapshots do not establish current circulation or reader rights.
No unions/branches double counted; no authentication, challenge/TLS bypass, reservations, outreach or app changes.
BNP query failed despite HTTP 200; UNA home, search-index snippets, filters and repositories not counted as successful searches.
Some source claims retained as indexed official/primary evidence with no downloaded body. Dates uncertain where explicitly indicated.
